parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows recent, quantified state action against trans women: 84 arrests/prosecutions (mainly gay men and trans women) in a four-month 2024–25 morality sweep, mass convictions up to 4.5 years upheld on appeal in Feb 2025, plus Article 230 enforcement with beatings and forced anal examinations (refusal treated as guilt). Custody is a state-imposed exposure: prisons process trans women under former names and birth gender systemically (Nov 2024). Official framing treats homosexuality as perversion. No trans-specific protections, remedies, or shelter machinery are documented; the 2017 anti-torture pledge was not honoured (tests ordered through 2019). Imprisonment after discovery is a realistic, documented pathway.

entry_documents.exposure: Outing through documents, appearance or accompaniment can trigger morality/debauchery charges; trans women are named in the 2024–25 sweep. No border-specific trans rule documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document or presentation mismatch → arrest under Art. 226 → prison identity refusal by birth sex.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arbitrary detention, beatings, forced confessions and coerced anal examinations documented; refusal treated as evidence of guilt; systemic processing under former names/birth gender in detention records, arrest and hearings (Nov 2024).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2017 ministerial pledge against forced tests — breached: courts kept ordering exams through 2018–19; outcome unresolved thereafter.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention record → birth-sex identity carried through court and prison, compounding outing and exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison placement/records by birth sex is systemic for trans women; a visitor convicted faces the same custody pipeline.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Arrest → detention records → hearings → prison, all under former name and birth gender.

care_services.exposure: Forced anal examinations as investigative/forensic procedure constitute intrusive, non-consensual medical procedure in custody.
care_services.protection: Pledge to stop forced testing exists but courts continued ordering exams through 2019; no later ruling documented.
care_services.interaction: Medical personnel become instruments of state investigation; refusal incriminates.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official statements call homosexuality perversion/illness requiring treatment and support punishment; Art. 226 applied to gender expression; morality sweeps named as targeting trans women.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented — no official statement on societal tolerance of transgender people appears in the inventory.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat-framing legitimises sweeps and reduces restraint during arrest and custody.

minors_guardians.exposure: A 16-year-old was jailed in 2017 for homosexuality after refusing an examination, showing minors face the same custody pipeline; a parent travelling with a trans minor or an outed trans parent faces family/child-protection scrutiny.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's examination refusal → short custody; accompanying adult's outing → same morality charges, leaving the child exposed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Sources record family rejection, public-space violence and suicides as 'common' without figures or dates; scale unestablished. Police are perpetrators (beatings, forced exams, coerced confessions).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented — no trans-specific hate-crime recourse described.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police hostility removes the usual recourse channel after street incidents.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Appeal court upheld the mass convictions (Feb 2025); LGR unsettled court-by-court with contradictory precedent; no shelter, victim-protection or visitor-specific machinery described.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Some sentence reductions (four released); formal courts accept appeals; pledges on forced testing exist on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Formal remedies exist but record shows them failing — upheld convictions, continued exams after pledge.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: active morality-law arrests of visitors/presenting people, prolonged custody with beatings and coerced confessions, courts deferring to security services, formal appeals largely illusory, a capital provision not applied to presentation cases. This dossier lacks a capital clause but adds a recent quantified crackdown (84 in four months) and upheld mass convictions, offsetting that difference.

Lower-rated anchor is milder: brief fines/short jail, annulled cases on appeal, no lethal-threat analogue. Here convictions are recent and upheld, forced examinations and custodial identity refusal are documented, and there is no record of courts restraining enforcement — so this jurisdiction sits materially below the 0.25 tier.

Much lower than this exclusion-only anchor: Vellandra's register produces refusal and humiliation without arrest. This dossier documents criminal charges, prison terms up to 4.5 years, coercive bodily examinations and systemic custodial misgendering — imprisonment, not exclusion, follows discovery.

parsed.synthesis: Law, enforcement and official framing align against the traveller. Active criminalisation (Art. 230, up to 3 years) plus Art. 226 applied to gender expression means discovery or suspicion leads to arrest; the 2024–25 sweep (84 arrested, mainly trans women and gay men, mass convictions upheld Feb 2025) shows this is current, not historical. Custody compounds harm: forced anal examinations (refusal = guilt), beatings, coerced confessions, and systemic processing of trans women under former names and birth gender through detention, trial and prison. The 2017 anti-torture pledge was breached. No trans-specific protection, shelter or remedy machinery is documented; recognition is unsettled. A trans traveller — alone or with a minor, who faces the same pipeline (a 16-year-old jailed in 2017) — confronts documented imprisonment with abusive custody and no working recourse.
